unit: fraction of the canvas short side

definitions.safeArea: The edge band, as a fraction of the short side, that text, the selo and the folio stay out of, because a feed, a trim or a projector can cover it. Only fields of colour, the cube motif and image slots enter it, and bleed off the edge.
definitions.bleed: Print only: how far, as a fraction of the short side, a full-bleed field, motif or image must extend past the trim edge so a cut never leaves a white sliver (3 mm on A4 and A3 is 0.014 and 0.01). A screen render is the trimmed size.
definitions.maxHeadlineChars: The most characters a headline set at the h1 size may have: about three lines of Montserrat 800 (0.56 em per character) across the text measure, which is the canvas width minus both margins. Shorten the copy; never shrink the type.
definitions.maxDisplayChars: The same limit for a headline set at the display size, which is larger and so holds fewer characters per line.
definitions.gridColumns: Every format uses a twelve-column grid. The archetypes place things in columns of twelve.

formats.label: Slide 16:9 (1920×1080)
formats.note: Read from the back of a room: body never below 2% of the short side, one idea per slide, so the word cap is low.

formats.label: Slide 4:3 (1440×1080)
formats.note: Same short side as 16:9, so the same type fractions; the narrower canvas favours one column over a split.

formats.label: A4 portrait (210×297 mm)
formats.note: Read at arm's length: body ≈10 pt, caption ≈8 pt is the floor. Generous 21 mm margins keep trim and binding safe.

formats.label: A3 portrait (297×420 mm)
formats.note: Read from a few metres: body ≈17 pt and a headline near 60 pt. A poster is a headline and one supporting block, not a page.

formats.label: Social square (1080×1080)
formats.note: Read on a phone in a feed: type is large relative to the canvas and copy is a headline plus one line.

formats.label: Social portrait (1080×1350)
formats.note: Same as the square, with a deeper safe area because feeds crop and overlay the top and bottom edges.

formats.label: Report cover (A4 portrait)
formats.note: A cover is a title, a subtitle and the selo: oversized display type with the page left mostly empty.
